# Reinforcement learning

For new RL, RLVR or GRPO work with supported Olmo MoE models, use
`python -m open_instruct.miles` and follow [the MILES guide](docs/miles/grpo.md),
including its launch checks and configuration conventions. Existing Core/vLLM
(`grpo.py`) and DeepSpeed/vLLM (`grpo_fast.py`) workflows remain current alternatives
for dense-model training; see [their guide](docs/algorithms/grpo.md).
Choose according to model and workload support, preserve the user's selected
workflow, and identify support gaps explicitly. MILES does not deprecate the
existing GRPO trainers.

For MILES GPU runs on `ai2/jupiter` or `ai2/saturn` (CUDA 12.8 host drivers), keep
the pinned MILES image: RunSpec defaults `launch.env.LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to the image's
CUDA compatibility libraries, and an explicit value wins. Revalidate CUDA
initialization and a short training run when the image or driver changes. See
[Jupiter CUDA compatibility](docs/miles/launching.md#jupiter-cuda-compatibility).

# Bash commands
- `uv run pytest`: Run the tests.
- `make style && make quality` run the linter + formatter.
- `uv run mkdocs serve`: View the documentation locally at http://127.0.0.1:8000/
- `uv run mkdocs build`: Build the documentation to the `site/` directory.



## Code Review Rules

Read and follow [CODE_REVIEW.md](CODE_REVIEW.md) when reviewing code.

# Workflow
- Begin every GitHub comment published by an agent with one plain line naming the agent (e.g. Codex, Claude Code): `Drafted by {agent name}.`, with no alert or other formatting. If a person reviewed the response before publication, use `Drafted by {agent name} and reviewed by {reviewer's name}.` instead. Only include the review attribution when that person actually reviewed the response; permission to post alone does not count as review.
- When a PR changes anything under `open_instruct/`, add a summary to `CHANGELOG.md` with a link to the PR (e.g., `- Description of change (https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/123).`). This is what CI enforces; PRs touching only `scripts/`, docs, or config are exempt, though an entry is still welcome for anything user-visible.
  - The entry must contain the PR's own URL, which does not exist until the PR is opened. Add the entry, open the PR, then amend the entry with the URL and push again.
  - To skip the check deliberately, put `CHANGELOG=<reason>` in the PR body.
- Always run the linter and make sure the tests pass before finishing a task.
- Prefer running single tests, not the whole suite, when developing.
- Launch Beaker experiment and test scripts with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh [--cuda-version 12|13] SCRIPT` after committing all changes. CUDA 13 images are for compatible clusters such as `ai2/holmes`. MILES uses `--miles CONFIG` and its pinned runtime.
- For the Core/vLLM and DeepSpeed/vLLM GRPO workflows, we have three test scripts (for MILES checks, follow `docs/miles/architecture.md`):
  - `scripts/train/debug/single_gpu_on_beaker.sh`: single GPU, no tools (~8 minutes).
  - `scripts/train/debug/tools/olmo_3_parser_multigpu.sh`: multi GPU, with tools.
  - `scripts/train/debug/large_test_script.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes, no tools (~32 minutes).
- For OLMo-core SFT, we have two test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft_multinode.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- For DPO, we have three test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/local.sh`: local single GPU (no Beaker).
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/single_gpu.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/multi_node.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- Launch the GPU tests with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`.
- CI runs on GitHub-hosted runners without Beaker experiments or image publication. Run GPU tests manually when a change touches GPU code paths. Record `GPU_TESTS=[EXPERIMENT_ID](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)` in the PR body for reviewers; CI does not parse or verify this line, and `GPU_TESTS=bypass` has no effect. The experiment must actually run `scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`; record training/debug smoke runs separately. Existing `open_instruct_auto*` images are no longer refreshed by CI; build from the intended revision with the launcher.
- If you are given a Beaker URL (`beaker.org` or `beaker.allen.ai`), use the Beaker CLI tool to interact with it.
- When a Beaker job stays queued or pending, run `beaker job events <job-id>` before diagnosing why — it prints the scheduler's own reason; don't infer one from cluster documentation. If that reason is the workspace slot limit, it applies to every cluster at once: wait or request fewer GPUs rather than relaunching elsewhere.
- A Beaker experiment can hold several jobs when a preempted one is retried. Read the most recently created attempt for each task and replica rank, not `jobs[0]` or one latest job for the entire experiment, or a successful retry looks like a failure and missing replicas can be overlooked.
- Mason's `--min_runtime <duration>` sets Beaker's `minRuntime` (0, or a duration with a unit of at least 5m, such as `30m`; Ai2 clusters currently allow at most 8h), and `--auto_resume` sets `autoResume`. On allocation-scheduled clusters, a job with a min runtime above 0 is allocated: it queues ahead of backfill and is protected until its min runtime ends, and shorter min runtimes schedule sooner. Its workspace needs an allocation on that cluster, or Beaker rejects it at submission. The legacy `--preemptible` switch, which cannot be combined with `--min_runtime`, maps to `minRuntime: 0` and `autoResume: true`; such unallocated jobs run only as backfill and may wait indefinitely. Passing neither flag maps to an eight-hour protected, non-resumable job, the hardest kind to schedule. Prefer a realistic `--min_runtime` (the time the job needs to reach a checkpoint), and call out this choice before launching instead of silently copying a checked-in script's choice.
- On macOS, GRPO launch scripts that call `mason.py` need `--no_auto_dataset_cache` (before the `--` separator). Local dataset caching runs the training entrypoint with `--cache_dataset_only`, and `grpo.py` / `grpo_fast.py` still import vllm at module level (`grpo_fast.py` from `vllm.distributed.weight_transfer`, `grpo.py` via `vllm_utils`), which is not installed on Darwin. `finetune.py`, `dpo.py`, `dpo_tune_cache.py` and `reward_modeling.py` no longer import vllm on this path since [#1866](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/1866), so their scripts do not need the flag. `mason.py` prints a macOS hint but still attempts caching, so it does not protect you either way.
- The `oe-eval-internal` directory is required in the Docker image for experiments that use `--try_launch_beaker_eval_jobs_on_weka`. If it's missing (e.g. in a fresh clone or worktree), clone it with: `git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/allenai/oe-eval-internal.git oe-eval-internal`.
- When updating PR bodies with experiment results, use the "Runs:" format (numbered list with Beaker links):
  ```
  Runs:

  1. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  2. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  ```

# Naming conventions
- Models OLMo and OLMo 2 (versions <=2) use the "OLMo" capitalization style.
- Olmo 3, Olmo Hybrid, and later models use "Olmo" (standard proper noun capitalization).
- Note: "OLMo-core" refers to the software repository and keeps its original capitalization.

# Coding conventions
- Never use `import logging` or `logging.info()` directly. Always use `logger = logger_utils.setup_logger(__name__)` and `logger.info()`.
- Imports always go at the top of the file, never inline.
- Use `from package import module` instead of `import package.module`.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.

tools.name: ReportFindings

Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

# Reinforcement learning

For new RL, RLVR or GRPO work with supported Olmo MoE models, use
`python -m open_instruct.miles` and follow [the MILES guide](docs/miles/grpo.md),
including its launch checks and configuration conventions. Existing Core/vLLM
(`grpo.py`) and DeepSpeed/vLLM (`grpo_fast.py`) workflows remain current alternatives
for dense-model training; see [their guide](docs/algorithms/grpo.md).
Choose according to model and workload support, preserve the user's selected
workflow, and identify support gaps explicitly. MILES does not deprecate the
existing GRPO trainers.

For MILES GPU runs on `ai2/jupiter` or `ai2/saturn` (CUDA 12.8 host drivers), keep
the pinned MILES image: RunSpec defaults `launch.env.LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to the image's
CUDA compatibility libraries, and an explicit value wins. Revalidate CUDA
initialization and a short training run when the image or driver changes. See
[Jupiter CUDA compatibility](docs/miles/launching.md#jupiter-cuda-compatibility).

# Bash commands
- `uv run pytest`: Run the tests.
- `make style && make quality` run the linter + formatter.
- `uv run mkdocs serve`: View the documentation locally at http://127.0.0.1:8000/
- `uv run mkdocs build`: Build the documentation to the `site/` directory.



## Code Review Rules

Read and follow [CODE_REVIEW.md](CODE_REVIEW.md) when reviewing code.

# Workflow
- Begin every GitHub comment published by an agent with one plain line naming the agent (e.g. Codex, Claude Code): `Drafted by {agent name}.`, with no alert or other formatting. If a person reviewed the response before publication, use `Drafted by {agent name} and reviewed by {reviewer's name}.` instead. Only include the review attribution when that person actually reviewed the response; permission to post alone does not count as review.
- When a PR changes anything under `open_instruct/`, add a summary to `CHANGELOG.md` with a link to the PR (e.g., `- Description of change (https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/123).`). This is what CI enforces; PRs touching only `scripts/`, docs, or config are exempt, though an entry is still welcome for anything user-visible.
  - The entry must contain the PR's own URL, which does not exist until the PR is opened. Add the entry, open the PR, then amend the entry with the URL and push again.
  - To skip the check deliberately, put `CHANGELOG=<reason>` in the PR body.
- Always run the linter and make sure the tests pass before finishing a task.
- Prefer running single tests, not the whole suite, when developing.
- Launch Beaker experiment and test scripts with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh [--cuda-version 12|13] SCRIPT` after committing all changes. CUDA 13 images are for compatible clusters such as `ai2/holmes`. MILES uses `--miles CONFIG` and its pinned runtime.
- For the Core/vLLM and DeepSpeed/vLLM GRPO workflows, we have three test scripts (for MILES checks, follow `docs/miles/architecture.md`):
  - `scripts/train/debug/single_gpu_on_beaker.sh`: single GPU, no tools (~8 minutes).
  - `scripts/train/debug/tools/olmo_3_parser_multigpu.sh`: multi GPU, with tools.
  - `scripts/train/debug/large_test_script.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes, no tools (~32 minutes).
- For OLMo-core SFT, we have two test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/oc_sft_multinode.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- For DPO, we have three test scripts:
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/local.sh`: local single GPU (no Beaker).
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/single_gpu.sh`: single GPU on Beaker.
  - `scripts/train/debug/dpo/multi_node.sh`: two 8x GPU nodes on Beaker.
- Launch the GPU tests with `./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`.
- CI runs on GitHub-hosted runners without Beaker experiments or image publication. Run GPU tests manually when a change touches GPU code paths. Record `GPU_TESTS=[EXPERIMENT_ID](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)` in the PR body for reviewers; CI does not parse or verify this line, and `GPU_TESTS=bypass` has no effect. The experiment must actually run `scripts/test/run_gpu_pytest.sh`; record training/debug smoke runs separately. Existing `open_instruct_auto*` images are no longer refreshed by CI; build from the intended revision with the launcher.
- If you are given a Beaker URL (`beaker.org` or `beaker.allen.ai`), use the Beaker CLI tool to interact with it.
- When a Beaker job stays queued or pending, run `beaker job events <job-id>` before diagnosing why — it prints the scheduler's own reason; don't infer one from cluster documentation. If that reason is the workspace slot limit, it applies to every cluster at once: wait or request fewer GPUs rather than relaunching elsewhere.
- A Beaker experiment can hold several jobs when a preempted one is retried. Read the most recently created attempt for each task and replica rank, not `jobs[0]` or one latest job for the entire experiment, or a successful retry looks like a failure and missing replicas can be overlooked.
- Mason's `--min_runtime <duration>` sets Beaker's `minRuntime` (0, or a duration with a unit of at least 5m, such as `30m`; Ai2 clusters currently allow at most 8h), and `--auto_resume` sets `autoResume`. On allocation-scheduled clusters, a job with a min runtime above 0 is allocated: it queues ahead of backfill and is protected until its min runtime ends, and shorter min runtimes schedule sooner. Its workspace needs an allocation on that cluster, or Beaker rejects it at submission. The legacy `--preemptible` switch, which cannot be combined with `--min_runtime`, maps to `minRuntime: 0` and `autoResume: true`; such unallocated jobs run only as backfill and may wait indefinitely. Passing neither flag maps to an eight-hour protected, non-resumable job, the hardest kind to schedule. Prefer a realistic `--min_runtime` (the time the job needs to reach a checkpoint), and call out this choice before launching instead of silently copying a checked-in script's choice.
- On macOS, GRPO launch scripts that call `mason.py` need `--no_auto_dataset_cache` (before the `--` separator). Local dataset caching runs the training entrypoint with `--cache_dataset_only`, and `grpo.py` / `grpo_fast.py` still import vllm at module level (`grpo_fast.py` from `vllm.distributed.weight_transfer`, `grpo.py` via `vllm_utils`), which is not installed on Darwin. `finetune.py`, `dpo.py`, `dpo_tune_cache.py` and `reward_modeling.py` no longer import vllm on this path since [#1866](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/1866), so their scripts do not need the flag. `mason.py` prints a macOS hint but still attempts caching, so it does not protect you either way.
- The `oe-eval-internal` directory is required in the Docker image for experiments that use `--try_launch_beaker_eval_jobs_on_weka`. If it's missing (e.g. in a fresh clone or worktree), clone it with: `git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/allenai/oe-eval-internal.git oe-eval-internal`.
- When updating PR bodies with experiment results, use the "Runs:" format (numbered list with Beaker links):
  ```
  Runs:

  1. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  2. Description: [Beaker](https://beaker.org/ex/EXPERIMENT_ID)
  ```

# Naming conventions
- Models OLMo and OLMo 2 (versions <=2) use the "OLMo" capitalization style.
- Olmo 3, Olmo Hybrid, and later models use "Olmo" (standard proper noun capitalization).
- Note: "OLMo-core" refers to the software repository and keeps its original capitalization.

# Coding conventions
- Never use `import logging` or `logging.info()` directly. Always use `logger = logger_utils.setup_logger(__name__)` and `logger.info()`.
- Imports always go at the top of the file, never inline.
- Use `from package import module` instead of `import package.module`.

# Documentation
To verify that documentation changes don't alter the generated output:

148	  { index = "pytorch-cu130", group = "cuda13" },

163	default-groups = ["dev", "cuda12"]   # uv sync 默认装 dev + cuda12

166	]

234	### 4.2 Dockerfile 构建入口
235	
236	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
237	
238	训练大模型通常不在笔记本上跑，而是提交到 GPU 集群（open-instruct 默认对接 Allen AI 的 Beaker）。集群环境不可控，所以要把「操作系统 + CUDA 工具链 + Python 依赖 + 仓库代码」整体打包成 Docker 镜像。open-instruct 的 `Dockerfile` 有两个鲜明特点：
239	
240	1. **一个文件支持两代 CUDA**：用多阶段构建 + 构建参数，`docker build --build-arg CUDA_VERSION=12` 或 `13` 出不同的镜像。
241	2. **镜像内用 uv 装依赖**：镜像里不手写 pip 命令，而是复用 4.1 节的同一套 `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`，做到「本地环境和镜像环境来自同一份声明」。
242	
243	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
244	
245	镜像构建流程：
246	
247	```text
248	docker build --build-arg CUDA_VERSION=12|13 .
249	    ↓
250	选择基础镜像：nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 或 13.0.3-devel-ubuntu22.04
251	    ↓
252	apt 安装基础工具（git/make/curl/nginx 等）
253	    ↓
254	安装 DOCA OFED 用户态驱动、Google Cloud CLI、Beaker CLI
255	    ↓
256	拷入 uv 可执行文件（官方镜像 ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv）
257	    ↓
258	uv run --frozen --no-default-groups --group dev --group cuda${CUDA_VERSION}
259	    → 按 uv.lock 精确安装依赖 + 下载 nltk 数据
260	    ↓
261	COPY 仓库代码（configs/scripts/mason.py/open_instruct/oe-eval-internal）
262	    ↓
263	设置 PATH 指向 /stage/.venv/bin，容器内命令直接可用
264	```
265	
266	#### 4.2.3 源码精读
267	
268	**① 双 CUDA 阶段选择**
269	
270	[Dockerfile:L1-L4](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L1-L4)：
271	
272	```dockerfile
273	ARG CUDA_VERSION=12
274	FROM nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 AS cuda12
275	FROM nvidia/cuda:13.0.3-devel-ubuntu22.04 AS cuda13
276	FROM cuda${CUDA_VERSION}
277	```
278	
279	前三行各定义一个阶段，最后一行用变量选择从哪个阶段继续构建——这是 Docker 的「条件基础镜像」惯用法。默认值是 12，AI2 的 Jupiter/Saturn 集群（CUDA 12.8 宿主驱动）就用默认；Holmes 等新集群用 `--build-arg CUDA_VERSION=13`。
280	
281	**② 基础工具与集群设施**
282	
283	[Dockerfile:L12-L22](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L12-L22) 安装 build-essential、git、make、nginx 等基础工具；[Dockerfile:L54-L64](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L54-L64) 安装固定版本（v1.5.235）的 Beaker CLI，供集群上提交任务使用。这些与 Python 无关，却是集群可运行性的保障。
284	
285	**③ 拷入 uv 并装配依赖**
286	
287	[Dockerfile:L66](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L66) 从官方镜像拷入 uv 0.8.6（CI 的 [tests.yml:L25-L27](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/.github/workflows/tests.yml#L25-L27) 也用同一版本，保持一致）。随后是整个镜像最核心的一步：
288	
289	[Dockerfile:L76-L80](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L76-L80)：
290	
291	```dockerfile
292	RUN --mount=type=cache,target=${UV_CACHE_DIR} \
293	    --mount=type=bind,source=uv.lock,target=uv.lock \
294	    --mount=type=bind,source=pyproject.toml,target=pyproject.toml \
295	    uv run --frozen --no-default-groups --group dev --group cuda${CUDA_VERSION} \
296	        python -m nltk.downloader punkt punkt_tab words
297	```
298	
299	这段做了三件事：
300	
301	- 用 `--frozen` 严格按 `uv.lock` 安装（代码改动不会引起依赖漂移）；
302	- 用 `--no-default-groups` **关掉**默认组，再显式指定 `--group dev --group cuda${CUDA_VERSION}`——因为默认组固定是 cuda12，而镜像需要按构建参数在 cuda12/cuda13 之间切换；
303	- 顺手下载 nltk 的分词数据（`punkt punkt_tab words`），数学判分等模块要用。
304	
305	注意这里只 bind-mount 了 `uv.lock` 和 `pyproject.toml`，**还没拷贝任何源码**——依赖层和代码层分离，代码改动时依赖层缓存依然有效，这是镜像构建加速的关键技巧。
306	
307	**④ 代码层与环境变量**

309	[Dockerfile:L83-L87](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L83-L87) 拷贝仓库代码。其中 `COPY oe-eval-interna[l] oe-eval-internal/` 的方括号是 Docker 的 glob 技巧：目录存在时正常拷贝，不存在时也不让构建失败（CLAUDE.md 说明该目录是 `--try_launch_beaker_eval_jobs_on_weka` 实验所必需，缺失时需自行 clone）。[Dockerfile:L89-L94](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L89-L94) 把 git 提交号写进环境变量，并把 `/stage/.venv/bin` 放进 PATH——容器里直接敲 `python` 就是刚装好的环境。

348	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
349	
350	研究代码库最怕「每个人一套风格」。open-instruct 用一个 28 行的 Makefile 把格式化、静态检查、测试统一成两条命令：
351	
352	- `make style`：**格式化**（自动改写你的代码排版）；
353	- `make quality`：**质量检查**（lint 自动修复 + 语法编译检查 + 类型检查）。
354	
355	配套还有 `-check` 变体（`style-check` / `quality-check`）：不改文件、只报告问题并以非零退出码失败，供 CI 使用。此外仓库用 pre-commit 把同样的检查挂到 `git commit` 上，用根目录 `conftest.py` 让 pytest 在缺少 vllm/GPU 的机器上自动跳过相关测试。
356	
357	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
358	
359	```text
360	开发者改完代码
361	    ↓
362	make style            → ruff format 改写排版（可能修改文件）
363	make quality          → ① check-keywords：确认没有违禁关键字 nonlocal
364	                        ② ruff check --fix：lint 并自动修复
365	                        ③ python -m compileall：语法编译检查
366	                        ④ ty check：类型检查
367	    ↓
368	uv run pytest         → conftest.py 先探测 vllm / CUDA 可用性
369	                        → 不可用的测试文件加入 collect_ignore，自动跳过
370	    ↓
371	git commit            → pre-commit 钩子再跑一遍 ruff + 关键字检查
372	                        + uv.lock 变化时重新导出 requirements.txt
373	    ↓
374	CI（.github/workflows）→ uv sync --frozen 装环境 → uv run --frozen pytest
375	```
376	
377	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
378	
379	**① Makefile 的目标定义**
380	
381	[Makefile:L1-L9](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Makefile#L1-L9)：
382	
383	```makefile
384	.PHONY: style quality check-keywords
385	
386	# make sure to test the local checkout in scripts and not the pre-installed one (don't use quotes!)
387	export PYTHONPATH = open_instruct
388	
389	check_dirs := open_instruct *mason.py
390	
391	style:
392		uv run ruff format $(check_dirs)
393	```
394	
395	- `check_dirs` 限定检查范围：`open_instruct/` 目录和根目录的 `mason.py`（`*mason.py` 同样匹配 `test_mason.py`）。
396	- `export PYTHONPATH = open_instruct` 确保测试跑的是本地检出代码而非 pip 装的旧版。
397	
398	[Makefile:L11-L14](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Makefile#L11-L14) 定义 quality 门禁：
399	
400	```makefile
401	quality: check-keywords
402		uv run ruff check -q --fix $(check_dirs)
403		uv run python -m compileall -qq $(check_dirs)
404		uv run ty check
405	```
406	
407	注意 `quality` 依赖 `check-keywords`，会先跑它。[Makefile:L26-L28](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Makefile#L26-L28) 是这个特殊检查：
408	
409	```makefile
410	check-keywords:
411		@test -d open_instruct/
412		@grep -rn --include='*.py' -E 'nonlocal[[:space:]]' open_instruct/; test $$? -eq 1
413	```
414	
415	逻辑是：grep 查找 `nonlocal ` 关键字，要求其退出码为 1（即「什么都没找到」）——找到了反而算失败。`nonlocal` 在多进程/分布式训练代码里是雷区，所以干脆全面禁用。
416	
417	**② 提交前钩子与 CI 保持同一套规则**
418	
419	[.pre-commit-config.yaml:L20-L28](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/.pre-commit-config.yaml#L20-L28) 挂载 ruff 与 ruff-format 钩子（作用域同样是 `open_instruct/` 和 `*mason.py`）；[.pre-commit-config.yaml:L32-L37](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/.pre-commit-config.yaml#L32-L37) 的 `ban-keywords` 钩子直接复用 `make check-keywords`；[.pre-commit-config.yaml:L38-L43](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/.pre-commit-config.yaml#L38-L43) 的 `export-requirements` 钩子在 `uv.lock` 变化时自动重新导出 `requirements.txt`——这就是 4.1.3 里「该文件是自动生成的」的机制保障。
420	
421	CI 侧，[.github/workflows/tests.yml:L28-L35](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/.github/workflows/tests.yml#L28-L35) 展示了官方装配顺序：`uv sync --frozen` → 下载 nltk `punkt_tab` → `uv run --frozen pytest`。你在本地照着做，就能最大程度复现 CI 行为。
422	
423	**③ pytest 的环境自适应**
424	
425	[conftest.py:L5-L22](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/conftest.py#L5-L22)：根目录的 conftest 先试探 vllm 是否可导入、CUDA 是否可用，然后把依赖它们的测试文件追加进 `collect_ignore`。效果是：在 没有 GPU 的笔记本上 `uv run pytest` 也不会因 vllm/GPU 用例报错，它们被静默跳过。
426	
427	**④ 实践要用的测试文件**
428	
429	[open_instruct/test_math_utils.py:L8-L24](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/open_instruct/test_math_utils.py#L8-L24) 是仓库里最小的测试之一：用 `parameterized` 把 9 组「LaTeX 字符串归一化」输入塞进同一个断言，检验 `math_utils.strip_string` 能否把 `\frac 1 2`、`\left(...\right)`、`50\%` 等写法归一成统一形式（这是数学答案判分的基础，u6-l3 会展开）。它只依赖 CPU 和纯 Python，是验证环境的首选用例。
430	
431	#### 4.3.4 代码实践
432	
433	**实践目标**：跑通「测试 + 格式化 + 质量门禁」完整闭环，亲眼看到门禁拦截坏代码。
434	
435	**操作步骤**：
436	
437	1. 跑指定测试文件：
438	
439	   ```bash
440	   uv run pytest open_instruct/test_math_utils.py -v
441	   ```
442	
443	2. 跑格式化（注意：这一步**可能改写文件**，这是正常的）：
444	
445	   ```bash
446	   make style
447	   ```
448	
449	3. 跑质量门禁：
450	
451	   ```bash
452	   make quality
453	   ```
454	
455	4. 主动制造一个违规，观察门禁工作：新建 `open_instruct/_style_probe.py`，内容只有一行 `import os`（一个未使用的 import），再执行 `make quality`，然后删除该文件并重跑确认恢复绿色。
456	
457	**需要观察的现象**：
458	
459	- 第 1 步：`test_latex_normalization` 被 parameterized 展开成 **9 个**子用例（对应 L10-L20 的 9 行参数），全部 PASSED（待本地验证具体输出）；
460	- 第 2 步：ruff format 对干净仓库通常是 no-op，输出 `X files left unchanged` 之类；
461	- 第 3 步：四道检查依次通过，退出码 0；
462	- 第 4 步：ruff check 报出 `F401 unused-import`（或自动 fix 删掉这行），quality 以非零退出码失败——门禁确实在拦人。
463	
464	**预期结果**：1-3 步全绿；第 4 步演示了「坏代码进不了仓库」的原因。
465	
466	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
467	
468	**练习 1**：`make style` 和 `make style-check` 有什么区别？分别什么时候用？
469	**答案**：[Makefile:L8-L9](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Makefile#L8-L9) 的 `style` 会直接改写文件排版；[Makefile:L16-L17](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Makefile#L16-L17) 的 `style-check` 用 `--check --diff` 只报告不改写、有问题就失败退出。本地开发用前者，CI 用后者。
470	
471	**练习 2**：为什么在没有 GPU 的机器上 `uv run pytest` 不会因为 GPU 测试失败？
472	**答案**：根目录 [conftest.py:L13-L22](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/conftest.py#L13-L22) 在收集阶段检测 vllm 可用性与 `torch.cuda.is_available()`，把不满足条件的测试文件加入 `collect_ignore`，pytest 直接跳过收集。
473	
474	**练习 3**：如果你改了 `pyproject.toml` 里的依赖并 `uv lock`，`requirements.txt` 会自动更新吗？
475	**答案**：会（前提是你装了 pre-commit 并执行了提交）。[.pre-commit-config.yaml:L38-L43](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/.pre-commit-config.yaml#L38-L43) 的 `export-requirements` 钩子监听 `uv.lock` 变化并自动运行导出命令。不走 pre-commit 时需要手动执行该导出命令。
476	
477	## 5. 综合实践
478	
479	**任务：产出一份你自己的《open-instruct 环境体检报告》。**
480	
481	在你刚装好的环境里依次完成，并把结果填进表格：
482	
483	| 检查项 | 命令 | 你的记录 |
484	|---|---|---|
485	| Python 版本 | `uv run python -c "import sys; print(sys.version)"` | 应为 3.12.x |
486	| torch 及 CUDA 变体 | `uv run python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__)"` | 应含 cu128（默认 cuda12 组） |
487	| uv 装了哪些组 | 查看 `pyproject.toml` 的 `default-groups` 并对比 `.venv` 中是否有 pytest/ruff | dev + cuda12 |
488	| 单测结果 | `uv run pytest open_instruct/test_math_utils.py -v` | 9 passed（待本地验证） |
489	| 全量 CPU 测试（可选） | `uv run pytest`（约数分钟） | 记录 passed/skipped 数量 |
490	| 格式化 | `make style` | 记录改写了几个文件 |
491	| 质量门禁 | `make quality` | 退出码应为 0 |
492	| 门禁有效性验证 | 新增含未使用 import 的探针文件再跑 `make quality` | 应失败并报 F401 |
493	| 文档站（可选） | `uv run mkdocs serve` 后浏览器打开 http://127.0.0.1:8000/ | 能看到 Open Instruct 文档站 |
494	
495	做完后回答两个思考题（答案都在本讲源码里）：
496	
497	1. 如果明天要在 CUDA 13 的集群上跑实验，你的安装命令和 Docker 构建命令分别要怎么改？
498	2. `make quality` 里四道检查（关键字、lint、编译、类型）各自能拦截哪类错误？举一个其他三道拦不住、只有某一道能拦的例子。

500	（参考答案：1. `uv sync --group cuda13`，`./scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh --cuda-version 13 <script>`；2. 例如「调用了不存在的属性」只有 ty 能在运行前发现，ruff/compileall 都不管类型。）
501	
502	## 6. 本讲小结
503	
504	- open-instruct 用 **uv + `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`** 管理依赖：Python 钉死 3.12，默认装 `dev + cuda12` 两组，`cuda12`/`cuda13` 通过 `conflicts` 互斥、通过 `tool.uv.sources` 切换 torch/vllm 的 wheel 索引。

506	- **`requirements.txt` 是 `uv.lock` 的自动导出物**（pip 路线用），由 pre-commit 钩子保持同步，不要手改。

508	- **质量工具链三条命令**：`uv run pytest`（conftest 自动跳过缺 vllm/GPU 的用例）、`make style`（ruff format 改写排版）、`make quality`（关键字检查 + ruff lint + compileall + ty）。

512	
513	环境就绪后，建议：
514

516	2. 再下一讲 **u1-l4 跑通第一个训练**：用本讲装好的环境 + `build_image_and_launch.sh`，跑一次 debug 冒烟脚本，第一次见到真实的训练日志。
517	3. 提前浏览 [docs/get_started/installation.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/docs/get_started/installation.md) 与 [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/CONTRIBUTING.md) 的测试一节，本讲的 pytest/质量门禁结论在那里有官方口径。

# 环境搭建：uv、Docker 与开发工具链

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 用 `uv sync` 在本地装好 open-instruct 的完整开发环境，并说清楚它到底装了什么、为什么这么装。
2. 读懂 `pyproject.toml` 中的依赖分组（`dev` / `cuda12` / `cuda13`）与 `tool.uv.sources` 的 CUDA 版本切换机制，理解同一份依赖声明如何支撑不同 GPU 平台。
3. 读懂 `Dockerfile` 的双 CUDA 阶段构建，理解训练镜像为什么长这样。
4. 掌握日常开发三板斧：`uv run pytest` 跑测试、`make style` 格式化、`make quality` 过质量门禁，并知道它们背后分别是 ruff、ty、compileall 等哪些工具。

本讲不涉及任何模型训练，只解决一件事：**把环境搭对，把工具链用起来**。这是后面所有讲义的前置条件。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 依赖管理器：从 pip 到 uv

- **pip**：Python 最经典的包管理器，按 `requirements.txt` 逐个安装，但不负责「锁版本」和「建虚拟环境」。
- **虚拟环境（venv）**：一个隔离的 Python 解释器 + 依赖目录，避免不同项目之间依赖互相污染。传统流程是 `python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate`。
- **uv**：Astral 公司用 Rust 写的下一代 Python 包管理器，一条 `uv sync` 命令可以同时完成「下载指定版本的 Python 解释器 + 创建 `.venv` + 按 lock 文件精确安装所有依赖」，速度比 pip 快一个数量级。open-instruct 已经把 uv 作为主力安装方式（安装文档中标注为 preview）。
- **lock 文件（`uv.lock`）**：把「我想要 torch>=2.10」这种模糊声明解析成「装 torch 2.10.x 的某个具体 wheel 及其哈希」的精确快照。CI 和 Docker 构建都用 `--frozen` 模式，即「只按 lock 装，不许重新解析」，保证所有人环境一致。

### 2.2 Python、PyTorch 与 CUDA 的三角关系

深度学习环境最常见的坑：PyTorch 的 wheel（预编译包）是**按 CUDA 版本分别编译**的。同样是 `torch==2.10.0`，CUDA 12.8 的 Linux 版和 CUDA 13.0 的 Linux 版是两个不同的文件，来自不同的下载索引。所以「装哪个 torch」取决于「你的机器驱动支持哪代 CUDA」。open-instruct 用 uv 的**依赖分组（dependency groups）**把这两套 wheel 隔开，这是本讲的重点之一。

### 2.3 工具链里的每个工具是干什么的

| 工具 | 角色 | 一句话说明 |
|---|---|---|
| ruff | 格式化 + Lint | 用 Rust 写的超快工具，`ruff format` 管代码排版，`ruff check` 找坏味道（未用 import、可疑写法等） |
| ty | 类型检查 | Astral 的 Python 类型检查器，静态发现类型错误 |
| compileall | 语法检查 | 把所有 `.py` 编译成字节码，能抓到语法错误 |
| pytest | 测试框架 | 自动发现并运行 `test_*.py` 里的用例 |
| pre-commit | Git 钩子管理 | 在 `git commit` 前自动跑格式化和检查 |
| mkdocs | 文档站 | 把 `docs/` 渲染成可搜索的文档网站 |
| Docker / Beaker | 容器 / AI2 集群 | 把环境打包成镜像，在 GPU 集群上复现 |

### 2.4 一条重要提醒：文档会滞后，源码是真相

安装文档 `docs/get_started/installation.md` 开头写的是「Dockerfile 使用 Python 3.10」，还提到了一个 `Dockerfile.uv` 文件。但你核对当前仓库会发现：`pyproject.toml` 钉死的是 **Python 3.12**，仓库里也**只有 `Dockerfile` 一个 Dockerfile**（它本身就内置了 uv）。这是研究代码库的常态——文档更新赶不上代码。本讲会同时告诉你「文档怎么说」和「源码实际是什么」，并教你在两者冲突时以 `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` + `Dockerfile` 为准。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| [docs/get_started/installation.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/docs/get_started/installation.md) | 官方安装指南：pip / uv / Docker 三条路线 |
| [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml) | 项目元数据、依赖声明、uv 分组与索引、ruff/ty/pytest 配置，**本讲最核心的文件** |
| [uv.lock](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/uv.lock) | uv 生成的精确锁文件，Docker 与 CI 用 `--frozen` 模式消费它 |
| [requirements.txt](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/requirements.txt) | 由 `uv export` 自动导出，供 pip 路线使用，**不是手写的** |
| [Dockerfile](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile) | 训练镜像入口：双 CUDA 阶段 + uv 安装依赖 |
| [Makefile](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Makefile) | `make style` / `make quality` 等质量门禁目标 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

本讲拆成三个最小模块：

1. **依赖声明与 uv 分组**（`pyproject.toml` 为主）
2. **Dockerfile 构建入口**（镜像里如何复用同一套依赖声明）
3. **Makefile 质量工具链**（ruff / ty / pytest / pre-commit 如何串成门禁）

### 4.1 依赖声明与 uv 分组

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`pyproject.toml` 是现代 Python 项目的「身份证 + 装备清单」。open-instruct 在这一个文件里同时声明了：

- 项目叫什么、支持哪个 Python 版本；
- 运行训练需要哪些库（torch、transformers、vllm、deepspeed、ray……）；
- 这些库在不同平台（Linux/macOS、x86_64/arm64）上分别怎么装；
- 开发工具（pytest、ruff、ty）单独归入 `dev` 组，不污染运行时；
- CUDA 12 与 CUDA 13 两套互斥的 GPU 栈分别归入 `cuda12` / `cuda13` 组。

「分组」的好处：一台 CUDA 12.8 驱动的机器和一台 CUDA 13 的机器，用**同一份声明**、**不同的 `--group` 参数**就能装出各自可用的环境，且两组永远不会被同时装进一个环境（uv 的 `conflicts` 声明强制互斥）。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

`uv sync` 的决策链可以概括为：

```text
读取 pyproject.toml（声明）
    ↓
解析规则：
    - Python 版本必须满足 requires-python（==3.12.*）
    - 默认安装 default-groups = ["dev", "cuda12"]
    - cuda12 与 cuda13 互斥（conflicts）
    - torch/torchvision/torchaudio 的下载源按所在组切换：
        cuda12 组 → pytorch-cu128 索引
        cuda13 组 → pytorch-cu130 索引
    - 平台标记（marker）过滤：
        vllm、bitsandbytes、flash-attn 等不装到 macOS（Darwin）
    ↓
对照 uv.lock（精确版本与哈希）
    ↓
创建/更新 .venv，uv 自管 Python 3.12（python-preference = "only-managed"）
    ↓
安装 open-instruct 本身（可编辑安装）+ 所选组的全部依赖
```

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**① Python 版本与核心依赖**

[pyproject.toml:L1-L6](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L1-L6) 声明项目名并钉死 Python 版本为 3.12：

```toml
[project]
name = "open-instruct"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Train open, instruction-following language models"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = "==3.12.*"
```

注意 `dynamic = ["version"]`：版本号不写死在文件里，而是由 git 标签动态生成（见后文 setuptools_scm）。这就是为什么 Docker 构建时要设置 `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_OPEN_INSTRUCT` 环境变量兜底。

[pyproject.toml:L7-L55](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L7-L55) 是运行时依赖清单，几个值得留意的条目：

- [pyproject.toml:L32](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L32)：`"torch>=2.10.0"` —— 只写版本下限，具体装哪个 CUDA 变体由后面的 `tool.uv.sources` 决定。
- [pyproject.toml:L38](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L38)：`"vllm>=0.19.1; platform_system != 'Darwin'"` —— vllm 没有 macOS 版本，用平台标记排除。
- [pyproject.toml:L43-L45](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L43-L45)：`flash-attn`、`liger-kernel` 等同样带平台标记；`flash-attn` 在 Apple Silicon（aarch64）上也不装。

**② 版本动态生成**

[pyproject.toml:L57-L65](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L57-L65) 声明构建系统，并用 setuptools_scm 从 git 状态生成版本号写入 `open_instruct/_version.py`：

```toml
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools", "setuptools_scm>=8"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[tool.setuptools_scm]
write_to = "open_instruct/_version.py"
```

**③ CUDA 分组切换的核心：tool.uv.sources 与索引**

这是本模块最关键的一段。[pyproject.toml:L83-L97](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L83-L97) 为 torch 三件套按「组」指定下载索引：

```toml
torch = [
  { index = "pytorch-cu128", group = "cuda12" },
  { index = "pytorch-cu130", group = "cuda13" },
  { index = "pytorch-cu130", marker = "platform_system == 'Linux' and platform_machine == 'aarch64'" },
]
```

读法：当解析 `cuda12` 组时，torch 一律从 `pytorch-cu128` 索引（即 CUDA 12.8 wheel）获取；解析 `cuda13` 组时改从 `pytorch-cu130` 获取。这些索引定义在 [pyproject.toml:L105-L118](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L105-L118)，都是 `explicit = true` 的专用索引（不会用于解析其他包）。[pyproject.toml:L78-L81](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L78-L81) 对 `flash-attn` 用的是另一种写法——直接按组指向不同的预编译 wheel URL。[pyproject.toml:L99-L103](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L99-L103) 则说明 vllm 的 PyPI 官方 wheel 基于 CUDA 12.8，`+cu130` 构建只发布在专用 wheel 索引上，所以只有 cuda13 组需要换源。

**④ uv 全局行为**

[pyproject.toml:L136-L154](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L136-L154) 定义 uv 的全局行为，四行最有信息量：

```toml
[tool.uv]
preview = true
python-preference = "only-managed"   # 只用 uv 自己下载的 Python，不用系统 Python
default-groups = ["dev", "cuda12"]   # uv sync 默认装 dev + cuda12
conflicts = [
    [ { group = "cuda12" }, { group = "cuda13" } ],   # 两组互斥
]
```

也就是说，在一台普通 Linux 机器上裸跑 `uv sync`，你得到的是 **dev 工具 + CUDA 12.8 训练栈**；要装 CUDA 13 栈需要显式 `uv sync --group cuda13`（此时 uv 会拒绝同时带上 cuda12）。

**⑤ 三个依赖组的内容**

[pyproject.toml:L156-L184](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L156-L184)：

- `cuda12` 组（L157-L165）与 `cuda13` 组（L166-L173）：内容几乎相同（torch 三件套 + vllm + flash-attn 系列），区别只在 flash-attn-3 的 wheel 是 cu128 还是 cu130 构建。真正的版本切换靠前述 `tool.uv.sources` 完成。
- `dev` 组（L174-L184）：`pytest`、`ruff`、`ty`、`beaker-py`、`mkdocs-material`、`pre-commit` 等，全是开发工具，不进运行时环境也能跑训练。

**⑥ requirements.txt 从哪来**

[requirements.txt:L1-L2](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/requirements.txt#L1-L2) 的第一行就自曝了身份：

```text
# This file was autogenerated by uv via the following command:
#    uv export --format requirements-txt --no-hashes --all-extras --group cuda12 --no-emit-project --output-file requirements.txt
```

它是从 `uv.lock` 导出的 cuda12 视图，供 pip 安装路线（[installation.md:L6-L16](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/docs/get_started/installation.md#L6-L16)）使用。pre-commit 里还有个钩子保证 `uv.lock` 变化时它会被重新导出（见 4.3.3）。**不要手改这个文件。**

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：用 `uv sync` 装好环境，并验证你装到的正是声明所描述的那套依赖。

**操作步骤**：

1. 确认已安装 uv（未安装可 `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`，这也是 [build_image_and_launch.sh:L102-L105](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh#L102-L105) 使用的安装方式）。
2. 在仓库根目录执行：

   ```bash
   uv sync
   ```

3. 验证解释器与关键库版本：

   ```bash
   uv run python -c "import sys; print(sys.version)"
   uv run python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__)"
   ```

4. 验证平台差异（在 Linux 上执行应成功；在 macOS 上执行应报 `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vllm'`，因为 L38 的标记把它排除了）：

   ```bash
   uv run python -c "import vllm; print(vllm.__version__)"
   ```

**需要观察的现象**：

- `uv sync` 首次运行会下载一个 uv 托管的 Python 3.12 并创建 `.venv/` 目录；
- `sys.version` 输出 3.12.x；
- `torch.__version__` 在 cuda12 默认组下应带 `cu128` 字样（具体小版本以 lock 为准，待本地验证）。

**预期结果**：所有命令退出码为 0（macOS 上第 4 步的报错本身也是「符合预期」的结果，说明平台标记生效）。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 torch 只写 `>=2.10.0`，而不直接在依赖里写死 CUDA 版本？
**答案**：因为同一个 torch 版本号对应多个按 CUDA 分别编译的 wheel。CUDA 变体的选择放在 [tool.uv.sources](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L83-L97) 里按依赖组切换：cuda12 组走 `pytorch-cu128` 索引，cuda13 组走 `pytorch-cu130` 索引。版本约束管「哪个版本」，source 管「哪个构建」。

**练习 2**：裸跑 `uv sync`（不带任何参数）会安装哪些组？
**答案**：`dev` 和 `cuda12`，因为 [pyproject.toml:L140](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L140) 设置了 `default-groups = ["dev", "cuda12"]`。所以本地开发开箱即得 pytest/ruff/ty 和 CUDA 12.8 栈。

**练习 3**：在一台 CUDA 13 集群的机器上应该怎么装环境？
**答案**：`uv sync --group cuda13`（dev 组仍是默认组之一会一起装上）。uv 的 `conflicts` 声明（[pyproject.toml:L141-L146](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/pyproject.toml#L141-L146)）保证 cuda12 与 cuda13 不会同时进入一个环境。

### 4.2 Dockerfile 构建入口

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

训练大模型通常不在笔记本上跑，而是提交到 GPU 集群（open-instruct 默认对接 Allen AI 的 Beaker）。集群环境不可控，所以要把「操作系统 + CUDA 工具链 + Python 依赖 + 仓库代码」整体打包成 Docker 镜像。open-instruct 的 `Dockerfile` 有两个鲜明特点：

1. **一个文件支持两代 CUDA**：用多阶段构建 + 构建参数，`docker build --build-arg CUDA_VERSION=12` 或 `13` 出不同的镜像。
2. **镜像内用 uv 装依赖**：镜像里不手写 pip 命令，而是复用 4.1 节的同一套 `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`，做到「本地环境和镜像环境来自同一份声明」。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

镜像构建流程：

```text
docker build --build-arg CUDA_VERSION=12|13 .
    ↓
选择基础镜像：nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 或 13.0.3-devel-ubuntu22.04
    ↓
apt 安装基础工具（git/make/curl/nginx 等）
    ↓
安装 DOCA OFED 用户态驱动、Google Cloud CLI、Beaker CLI
    ↓
拷入 uv 可执行文件（官方镜像 ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv）
    ↓
uv run --frozen --no-default-groups --group dev --group cuda${CUDA_VERSION}
    → 按 uv.lock 精确安装依赖 + 下载 nltk 数据
    ↓
COPY 仓库代码（configs/scripts/mason.py/open_instruct/oe-eval-internal）
    ↓
设置 PATH 指向 /stage/.venv/bin，容器内命令直接可用
```

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**① 双 CUDA 阶段选择**

[Dockerfile:L1-L4](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L1-L4)：

```dockerfile
ARG CUDA_VERSION=12
FROM nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 AS cuda12
FROM nvidia/cuda:13.0.3-devel-ubuntu22.04 AS cuda13
FROM cuda${CUDA_VERSION}
```

前三行各定义一个阶段，最后一行用变量选择从哪个阶段继续构建——这是 Docker 的「条件基础镜像」惯用法。默认值是 12，AI2 的 Jupiter/Saturn 集群（CUDA 12.8 宿主驱动）就用默认；Holmes 等新集群用 `--build-arg CUDA_VERSION=13`。

**② 基础工具与集群设施**

[Dockerfile:L12-L22](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L12-L22) 安装 build-essential、git、make、nginx 等基础工具；[Dockerfile:L54-L64](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L54-L64) 安装固定版本（v1.5.235）的 Beaker CLI，供集群上提交任务使用。这些与 Python 无关，却是集群可运行性的保障。

**③ 拷入 uv 并装配依赖**

[Dockerfile:L66](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L66) 从官方镜像拷入 uv 0.8.6（CI 的 [tests.yml:L25-L27](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/.github/workflows/tests.yml#L25-L27) 也用同一版本，保持一致）。随后是整个镜像最核心的一步：

[Dockerfile:L76-L80](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L76-L80)：

```dockerfile
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=${UV_CACHE_DIR} \
    --mount=type=bind,source=uv.lock,target=uv.lock \
    --mount=type=bind,source=pyproject.toml,target=pyproject.toml \
    uv run --frozen --no-default-groups --group dev --group cuda${CUDA_VERSION} \
        python -m nltk.downloader punkt punkt_tab words
```

这段做了三件事：

- 用 `--frozen` 严格按 `uv.lock` 安装（代码改动不会引起依赖漂移）；
- 用 `--no-default-groups` **关掉**默认组，再显式指定 `--group dev --group cuda${CUDA_VERSION}`——因为默认组固定是 cuda12，而镜像需要按构建参数在 cuda12/cuda13 之间切换；
- 顺手下载 nltk 的分词数据（`punkt punkt_tab words`），数学判分等模块要用。

注意这里只 bind-mount 了 `uv.lock` 和 `pyproject.toml`，**还没拷贝任何源码**——依赖层和代码层分离，代码改动时依赖层缓存依然有效，这是镜像构建加速的关键技巧。

**④ 代码层与环境变量**

[Dockerfile:L83-L87](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L83-L87) 拷贝仓库代码。其中 `COPY oe-eval-interna[l] oe-eval-internal/` 的方括号是 Docker 的 glob 技巧：目录存在时正常拷贝，不存在时也不让构建失败（CLAUDE.md 说明该目录是 `--try_launch_beaker_eval_jobs_on_weka` 实验所必需，缺失时需自行 clone）。[Dockerfile:L89-L94](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Dockerfile#L89-L94) 把 git 提交号写进环境变量，并把 `/stage/.venv/bin` 放进 PATH——容器里直接敲 `python` 就是刚装好的环境。

**⑤ 文档中已失效的引用**

[installation.md:L41-L49](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/docs/get_started/installation.md#L41-L49) 提到「用 `Dockerfile.uv` 构建带 uv 的镜像」，但当前仓库已经没有这个文件——因为主 `Dockerfile` 本身就内置了 uv（见上文 L66、L76-L80）。同样，[installation.md:L4](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/docs/get_started/installation.md#L4) 说「使用 Python 3.10」，而 `pyproject.toml` 已钉到 3.12。读文档时请以源码为准，这是研究仓库的生存技能。

#### 4.2.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：不真正构建镜像（耗时且需要网络），通过读脚本掌握 CUDA 版本如何一路传递；有 Docker 环境的读者可实际构建。

**操作步骤（阅读路线）**：

### 4.3 Makefile 质量工具链

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

研究代码库最怕「每个人一套风格」。open-instruct 用一个 28 行的 Makefile 把格式化、静态检查、测试统一成两条命令：

- `make style`：**格式化**（自动改写你的代码排版）；
- `make quality`：**质量检查**（lint 自动修复 + 语法编译检查 + 类型检查）。

配套还有 `-check` 变体（`style-check` / `quality-check`）：不改文件、只报告问题并以非零退出码失败，供 CI 使用。此外仓库用 pre-commit 把同样的检查挂到 `git commit` 上，用根目录 `conftest.py` 让 pytest 在缺少 vllm/GPU 的机器上自动跳过相关测试。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
开发者改完代码
    ↓
make style            → ruff format 改写排版（可能修改文件）
make quality          → ① check-keywords：确认没有违禁关键字 nonlocal
                        ② ruff check --fix：lint 并自动修复
                        ③ python -m compileall：语法编译检查
                        ④ ty check：类型检查
    ↓
uv run pytest         → conftest.py 先探测 vllm / CUDA 可用性
                        → 不可用的测试文件加入 collect_ignore，自动跳过
    ↓
git commit            → pre-commit 钩子再跑一遍 ruff + 关键字检查
                        + uv.lock 变化时重新导出 requirements.txt
    ↓
CI（.github/workflows）→ uv sync --frozen 装环境 → uv run --frozen pytest
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**① Makefile 的目标定义**

[Makefile:L1-L9](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Makefile#L1-L9)：

```makefile
.PHONY: style quality check-keywords

# make sure to test the local checkout in scripts and not the pre-installed one (don't use quotes!)
export PYTHONPATH = open_instruct

check_dirs := open_instruct *mason.py

style:
	uv run ruff format $(check_dirs)
```

- `check_dirs` 限定检查范围：`open_instruct/` 目录和根目录的 `mason.py`（`*mason.py` 同样匹配 `test_mason.py`）。
- `export PYTHONPATH = open_instruct` 确保测试跑的是本地检出代码而非 pip 装的旧版。

[Makefile:L11-L14](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Makefile#L11-L14) 定义 quality 门禁：

```makefile
quality: check-keywords
	uv run ruff check -q --fix $(check_dirs)
	uv run python -m compileall -qq $(check_dirs)
	uv run ty check
```

注意 `quality` 依赖 `check-keywords`，会先跑它。[Makefile:L26-L28](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/Makefile#L26-L28) 是这个特殊检查：

```makefile
check-keywords:
	@test -d open_instruct/
	@grep -rn --include='*.py' -E 'nonlocal[[:space:]]' open_instruct/; test $$? -eq 1
```

逻辑是：grep 查找 `nonlocal ` 关键字，要求其退出码为 1（即「什么都没找到」）——找到了反而算失败。`nonlocal` 在多进程/分布式训练代码里是雷区，所以干脆全面禁用。

**② 提交前钩子与 CI 保持同一套规则**

[.pre-commit-config.yaml:L20-L28](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/.pre-commit-config.yaml#L20-L28) 挂载 ruff 与 ruff-format 钩子（作用域同样是 `open_instruct/` 和 `*mason.py`）；[.pre-commit-config.yaml:L32-L37](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/.pre-commit-config.yaml#L32-L37) 的 `ban-keywords` 钩子直接复用 `make check-keywords`；[.pre-commit-config.yaml:L38-L43](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/.pre-commit-config.yaml#L38-L43) 的 `export-requirements` 钩子在 `uv.lock` 变化时自动重新导出 `requirements.txt`——这就是 4.1.3 里「该文件是自动生成的」的机制保障。

CI 侧，[.github/workflows/tests.yml:L28-L35](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/.github/workflows/tests.yml#L28-L35) 展示了官方装配顺序：`uv sync --frozen` → 下载 nltk `punkt_tab` → `uv run --frozen pytest`。你在本地照着做，就能最大程度复现 CI 行为。

**③ pytest 的环境自适应**

[conftest.py:L5-L22](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/conftest.py#L5-L22)：根目录的 conftest 先试探 vllm 是否可导入、CUDA 是否可用，然后把依赖它们的测试文件追加进 `collect_ignore`。效果是：在 没有 GPU 的笔记本上 `uv run pytest` 也不会因 vllm/GPU 用例报错，它们被静默跳过。

**④ 实践要用的测试文件**

[open_instruct/test_math_utils.py:L8-L24](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/896a734f5152f6092a1ae2c2bccb8195a70abc42/open_instruct/test_math_utils.py#L8-L24) 是仓库里最小的测试之一：用 `parameterized` 把 9 组「LaTeX 字符串归一化」输入塞进同一个断言，检验 `math_utils.strip_string` 能否把 `\frac 1 2`、`\left(...\right)`、`50\%` 等写法归一成统一形式（这是数学答案判分的基础，u6-l3 会展开）。它只依赖 CPU 和纯 Python，是验证环境的首选用例。

## 6. 本讲小结

- open-instruct 用 **uv + `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`** 管理依赖：Python 钉死 3.12，默认装 `dev + cuda12` 两组，`cuda12`/`cuda13` 通过 `conflicts` 互斥、通过 `tool.uv.sources` 切换 torch/vllm 的 wheel 索引。
- **平台差异用 marker 声明**：vllm、bitsandbytes、flash-attn 等不进 macOS 环境，一份声明适配多平台。
- **`requirements.txt` 是 `uv.lock` 的自动导出物**（pip 路线用），由 pre-commit 钩子保持同步，不要手改。
- **Dockerfile 一个文件出两代 CUDA 镜像**：`ARG CUDA_VERSION` 选基础镜像、选依赖组，依赖层与代码层分离以利用缓存；镜像内同样用 uv + `--frozen`，与本地同源。
- **质量工具链三条命令**：`uv run pytest`（conftest 自动跳过缺 vllm/GPU 的用例）、`make style`（ruff format 改写排版）、`make quality`（关键字检查 + ruff lint + compileall + ty）。
- **文档可能滞后**（Python 3.10 vs 3.12、不存在的 `Dockerfile.uv`），冲突时以 `pyproject.toml`、`uv.lock`、`Dockerfile` 为准。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).

- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.
